title: Why we schedule
blurb: State the purpose of scheduling: turning the work into a timed, sequenced plan you can coordinate and track.
question: A project manager has a work breakdown structure and estimates for every work package, but the team keeps asking when they should start and who they are waiting on. Which planning activity answers this, and what is its purpose?

teach.body: The WBS tells you WHAT work must be done. Estimates tell you HOW LONG each piece takes. Scheduling puts it all on a calendar: it works out the order of the activities, how long each takes and what resources each needs, then gives every activity a start and finish date. The result is the overall project duration and a timed plan everyone can work to.

Formally: scheduling determines when the work will be done, by sequencing activities through their dependencies, applying their durations and resource needs, and so producing start and finish dates and the overall duration, shown as a network diagram and/or a Gantt chart. In plain English: it answers 'what happens when, in what order, and with whom?'

teach.text: Scheduling answers WHEN. Exam distractors offer the job of another tool: defining the scope (WBS: what), assigning accountability (RAM: who), justifying the investment (business case: why) or costing the work (budget: how much). None of these is the purpose of scheduling.

items: Purpose: determine when the work will be done, giving start and finish dates and the overall duration.
Built from activities (WBS), dependencies, durations and resource needs.
Shown as a network diagram (logic) and/or a Gantt chart (bars on a calendar).
Lets the PM coordinate resources, find the critical path, baseline time and communicate key dates.
Once baselined, it is the yardstick for monitoring progress and forecasting completion.

summary: You can now state the purpose of scheduling: to determine when the work will be done by sequencing activities and applying durations and resources. You can also explain how a schedule helps coordinate resources, identify the critical path, baseline time and communicate key dates.

A.q: Which of the following best states the purpose of scheduling?
options: To determine when the work will be done
To define what work is within the scope
To decide who is accountable for work
To justify why the project is needed
A.why: Scheduling determines when the work will be done: the sequence, durations and resources, giving dates and the overall duration.

whyNot.1: Defining what work is in scope is the job of scope management and the WBS.
whyNot.2: Accountability for work is shown in a responsibility assignment matrix (RAM).
whyNot.3: Justifying the project is the purpose of the business case.

A.q: Complete the statement: a schedule is built by combining the activities with their dependencies, ______ and resource needs.
A.why: Activities, dependencies, durations and resource needs are the building blocks of a schedule.

whyNot.0: Benefits are tracked through benefits management, not used to time activities.
whyNot.1: Stakeholders are analysed for engagement; they are not a scheduling input in this sense.
whyNot.3: Risk owners appear in the risk register, not as a schedule building block.

A.q: Where does a scheduler normally get the list of activities to be sequenced?
A.why: The WBS breaks the work into work packages and activities, which the scheduler then sequences and times.

whyNot.0: The stakeholder register lists people and groups with an interest, not activities.
whyNot.2: The benefits plan covers how and when benefits are realised, not the work activities.
whyNot.3: The communication plan sets out who gets what information and how.

B.q: A Gantt chart for the Riverside Café refit shows every activity against a calendar. Which purpose of scheduling does this most directly support?
options: Justifying the cost of the refit
B.why: Bars on a calendar make it easy to see and share when each activity happens and when the project will finish.

whyNot.1: The cost justification belongs in the business case.
whyNot.2: Acceptance criteria are set through quality and requirements work, not the Gantt chart.
whyNot.3: Risk probability is assessed in risk management, not shown on a Gantt chart.

B.q:
Which TWO of the following are purposes of scheduling?
1. Identify the critical path
2. Approve the business case
3. Provide a time baseline for monitoring
4. Allocate the budget to cost accounts
B.why: Scheduling identifies the critical path and provides the time baseline against which progress is monitored.

whyNot.0: Approving the business case is a sponsor and governance decision, and allocating budget to cost accounts uses the CBS.
whyNot.1: Statement 2 is wrong: the business case is approved through governance, not by scheduling.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: budget allocation to cost accounts is done with the cost breakdown structure.

B.q: Once the schedule has been baselined, how does it help the project manager during deployment?
options: It removes the need for progress reports
It lets actual progress be compared to plan
It fixes the scope so no changes can occur
It sets the benefits to be realised later
B.why: The baselined schedule is the time yardstick: comparing actual dates with planned dates shows whether the project is ahead or behind.

whyNot.0: Progress reports are still needed; the schedule gives them something to report against.
whyNot.2: Scope can still change through change control; the schedule does not freeze it.
whyNot.3: Benefits are defined in the business case and managed through benefits management.

C.q: On an office move, IT asks when the network must be ready and facilities asks when furniture arrives. With no schedule, which problem is most likely?
options: Resources turn up at the wrong time
C.why: Coordinating resources is a core purpose of scheduling. Without dates and a sequence, people and deliveries arrive too early or too late.

whyNot.0: The business case justifies the project; a missing schedule doesn't by itself invalidate it.
whyNot.1: Stakeholders are identified through stakeholder analysis, not the schedule.
whyNot.3: Quality criteria can be agreed without a schedule; they are a quality matter.

C.q: Which of the following is NOT normally a direct output of scheduling?
options: Start and finish dates per activity
The critical path through the work
C.why: Appraising investment options is part of the business case. Dates, duration and the critical path all come out of scheduling.

whyNot.0: Start and finish dates are exactly what scheduling produces.
whyNot.1: The overall duration is a key output of scheduling.
whyNot.3: Scheduling with a network diagram identifies the critical path.

C.q: Complete the statement: compared with a network diagram, a Gantt chart ______.
options: shows the logic but gives no dates
is only used for iterative work
removes the need for a WBS
C.why: A Gantt chart shows each activity as a bar against a timescale, which makes dates easy to read and track.

whyNot.0: Logic without dates describes a network diagram, not a Gantt chart.
whyNot.1: Gantt charts are used in linear, iterative and hybrid projects alike.
whyNot.2: The activities on a Gantt chart still come from the WBS.

reteach.title: Think of cooking a Sunday roast
reteach.question: You have one oven, one cook and six dishes that must all be hot at 1 pm. How is planning the meal like scheduling a project?

blocks.body: You list the dishes (the activities), notice that the gravy needs the meat juices (a dependency), know the meat takes three hours (a duration) and that there's only one oven (a resource). Working backwards from 1 pm gives each dish a start time. That plan, and the clock you check it against while cooking, is a schedule.

blocks.caption: Each dish has a start time, the order is set by dependencies, and the serving time is fixed.

blocks.body: Scheduling does the same for a project: it decides when each activity happens so that people and equipment are used at the right time, everyone knows the key dates, and you can tell early if you are falling behind.

explain.body: The WBS covers what, the RAM covers who, estimates cover how long and how much. Scheduling brings them together into dates: the sequence of activities, their start and finish dates and the overall project duration.

test.why: Scheduling determines when the work will be done.

whyNot.0: What will be delivered is defined by the PBS and scope.
whyNot.1: Accountability is shown in the RAM.
whyNot.3: The reason for the project is set out in the business case.

explain.body: To build a schedule you need the activities, the dependencies between them, a duration for each and the resources each needs, plus any fixed dates. Miss one and the dates won't be realistic.

test.q: Which of the following is NOT an input to building a schedule?
test.why: A benefits review happens after outputs are in use; it does not feed the dates of activities.

whyNot.0: Durations are a core scheduling input.
whyNot.1: Dependencies set the sequence, so they are essential.
whyNot.2: Resource availability affects when work can actually happen.

explain.body: A network diagram shows the logic: boxes for activities, arrows for dependencies. A Gantt chart shows each activity as a bar on a calendar, which is the clearest way to tell a team when things happen.

test.q: Which schedule view is best for showing a team when each activity happens?
test.why: A Gantt chart shows activities as bars against a calendar, so dates are easy to read.

whyNot.1: A risk register records risks, not activity dates.
whyNot.3: A stakeholder map shows power and interest, not timing.

explain.body: Once agreed, the schedule becomes the time baseline. Each period the PM compares actual progress with it, forecasts the end date and takes corrective action early. Changes to the baseline go through change control.

test.q: Why does the schedule still matter once deployment has started?
options: It replaces the project management plan
It records the lessons learned so far
It is the time baseline to track progress
It sets the quality standards for outputs
test.why: The baselined schedule is what actual progress is measured against, so variances show up early.

whyNot.0: The schedule is part of the PMP; it doesn't replace it.
whyNot.1: Lessons are captured in a lessons log or report.
whyNot.3: Quality standards are set in the quality plan.
